Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached is the governance annex portion of our RFP — we are collecting focused responses around NIST AI RMF mappings, EU AI Act classification/mitigation, and the practical evaluation/regression cadence you would offer for a clinical scheduling assistant integration.

Two specific asks up front:

Also please describe your evaluation/regression approach when models (or model variants/quantizations) are updated: sampling strategy, metrics you track, regression gates and rollback triggers. We prefer a short deliverable we can attach to contract annexes (control matrix + evaluation cadence).

We have a budgeted timeline for this track — a firm response by next Tuesday (2026-08-10) would be ideal. Can we set a 30-minute call tomorrow afternoon to walk through?

On Mon, Aug 2, 2026 at 10:00 AM Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team — forwarding Luma's ask. Quick summary and proposed deliverables below.

Thanks — adding some technical specifics we should include in the evaluation/regression annex. High level bullets to convert into the deliverable:

- Evaluation harness: a reproducible test harness that runs a curated evaluation set (seed prompts + edge cases) against each model variant. Harness stores outputs, token-level latency, and per-example metadata in a results bundle (JSONL + metadata CSV).
- Regression sampling: stratified sampling by intent + entity sensitivity (medical vs scheduling only) with a minimum sample floor (e.g., 1k examples) for major model changes; continuous micro-sampling (e.g., 0.5% production traffic) for incremental releases.
- Metrics to track: task accuracy (where ground truth exists), factuality / hallucination score (LM-based evaluator + human adjudication for flagged examples), latency P95, token cost delta, safety/toxicity detectors, policy-violation rate.
- Gates & triggers: automatic hold if any of the following occur: + absolute increase in hallucination rate > 3 percentage points OR + drop in task accuracy > 5% OR + latency P95 increase > 60 ms on production-like traces.
- Canary & rollback: staged rollout with small canary cohort (1-5% traffic), automated rollback hook if regression metrics cross thresholds. Provide an audit trail of canary evaluation results in the console/dashboard.
- Evidence artifacts: evaluation bundles, sampling seed lists, model version manifest, KV-cache snapshots (as relevant), signed attestation from Redwood Engineering for release builds.

For EU AI Act: If Luma treats the integration as high-risk, we should propose:
- A conformity annex with (a) the control mapping, (b) test harness/metrics, (c) post-market monitoring plan, (d) transparency statement for end-users, and (e) human oversight design notes.
- Note: true conformity assessment usually requires a notified body for certain modules; Redwood can provide the technical dossier and evidence to support their conformity path but cannot act as the notified body. Legal should confirm the language.

I'll draft the evaluation annex section this morning and attach a sample metrics dashboard output.

- Aditya
Senior Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-draft-eval-annex-v1.pdf (draft, internal)
